chunks: I came across Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in one of the streets of Medina on a scorching summer day of intense heat.

I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Given your station with God the Mighty and Majestic, and your kinship to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), you are exerting yourself on such a day?'
He said: 'O Abd al-A'la! I have gone out in search of livelihood so that I may be self-sufficient from the likes of you.'

key_terms.الرِّزْق: Livelihood, sustenance, daily provision — encompassing both material earning and divinely allocated portion
key_terms.الِاسْتِغْنَاء: Self-sufficiency, being needless of others; the Imam frames seeking livelihood as a means to preserve personal dignity
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: Formulaic expression of veneration: 'May I be your sacrifice/ransom', used when addressing respected figures

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq work for his livelihood despite his high status?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts an encounter between a companion, Abd al-A'la, and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in the streets of Medina on an extremely hot day. The companion was surprised to see the Imam working hard under such conditions, given his exalted status with God and lineage to the Prophet. The Imam's response reveals a profound ethical principle: that even those of noble lineage and high spiritual station must work to earn their own livelihood and thereby preserve their dignity and independence from relying on others.
word_analysis: so that I may be self-sufficient / needless

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abdullah Bin Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdul A’ala a slave of the progeny of Saam who said, ‘I came across Abu Abdullah in one of the streets of Al-Medina during a scorching day of intense heat.

So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Your<sup>asws</sup> have a (prominent) status with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and nearness to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and you<sup>asws</sup> are striving for yourself<sup>asws</sup> in a day like this?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abdul A’ala! I<sup>asws</sup> have come out regarding seeking the livelihood in order to be needless from the likes of you’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ‘Abd Allah al-Dihqan from Durust from ‘Abd al-A’la’, Mawla’ Ale Sam who has said the following: “I once came face to face with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in one of the streets of al-Madinah on a very hot summer day.

I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, you have a prominent position before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, and you are of very close relatives of the Messenger of Allah and you are (not to be) striving in a day like this.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘O ‘Abd al-‘A‘la’, I came out in search for my sustenance so that I would not need to spread my hands before you (your fellow) humankind for help.’”
